extracted.intended_audience: Inventors, patent attorneys, patent-office officials, and legal practitioners interpreting U.S. patent statutes (historical statutes, esp. acts through 1837)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts statutory criteria and procedural requirements for obtaining, maintaining, examining, assigning, and reissuing patents under the cited U.S. Acts (late 18th–early 19th century), including office organization, fees, documentary and model requirements, examination and appeal processes, and remedies for infringement. Useful for understanding historical U.S. patent standards and administrative practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of patent privileges to aliens (residency requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Privileges given to citizens by the patent act are extended to aliens who, at the time of petitioning, shall have resided for two years within the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such aliens obtain and enjoy privileges under the same conditions, limitations and restrictions as citizens; every person petitioning pursuant to this extension must make oath or affirmation before some person authorized to administer oaths that the invention hath not, to the best of his or her knowledge or belief, been known or used either in this or any foreign country; any patent obtained under this act that is later shown to have been known or used previously shall be utterly void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of novelty and originality for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person petitioning for a patent shall make oath or affirmation that such invention, art, or discovery hath not, to the best of his or her knowledge or belief, been known or used either in this or any foreign country, and that the applicant verily believes he is the original and first inventor or discoverer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath may be made before any person authorized by law to administer oaths; if later it appears the subject had been previously known or used, the patent shall be void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of legal representatives of deceased inventors to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person hath made a new invention and shall die before any patent shall be granted, the right of applying for and obtaining such patent shall devolve on the legal representatives (executors/administrators) in trust for heirs at law or devisees as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When application is made by legal representatives, the oath/affirmation required shall be varied to be applicable to them; they hold the same conditions, limitations, and restrictions as the inventor would have held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for infringement — treble damages
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person, without the consent of the patentee or his executors, administrators or assigns, shall make, devise, use, or sell the patented thing, such person shall forfeit and pay to the patentee a sum equal to three times the actual damage sustained by reason of such offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such sum shall be recoverable by action on the case founded on the act, in the circuit court of the United States having jurisdiction thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circuit courts' original cognisance in patent cases; equitable relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The circuit courts of the United States shall have original cognisance, as well in equity as at law, of all actions, suits, controversies, and cases arising under any law of the United States granting or confirming exclusive rights to authors or inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On any bill in equity filed by an aggrieved party, the courts shall have authority to grant injunctions according to equity principles to prevent violation of rights secured by U.S. laws; appeals or writs of error to the Supreme Court lie from such judgments and decrees as in other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report and publication of expired patents
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be the duty of the Secretary of State, annually in January, to report to Congress and publish in two Washington newspapers a list of all patents for discoveries/inventions/improvements which shall have expired within the preceding year, with patentees' names alphabetically arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Congress to prolong or renew patent term (notice and verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application to Congress to prolong or renew a patent must be made before its expiration and be notified at least once a month for three months before presentation in two Washington newspapers and one newspaper of the State or territory of the patentee's residence; the petition shall set forth the grounds and be verified by oath; evidence may be taken before a judge or justice of the peace and must include a statement of ascertained value and receipts/expenditures to show profit or loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes procedural/ evidentiary requirements for Congressional extension petitions (publication, verification, financial disclosure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary may reissue patent for inadvertent noncompliance with formal terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is invalid or inoperative because terms/conditions prescribed in the earlier act's third section were not complied with by inadvertence, accident, or mistake and without fraudulent intention, the Secretary of State, upon surrender of such patent, may cause a new patent to be granted for the residue of the unexpired term upon compliance with required terms/conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New patent is liable to the same objections and defenses as an original patent; in case of death or assignment, same right vests in executors/assignees; public use after original grant does not prejudice recovery for uses after grant of the new patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileges for resident aliens declaring intent to naturalize; conditions to avoid voiding
rubrics_metrics.description: Privileges extended to aliens who are residents and have declared intention to become citizens; provided that any patent issued to such an alien shall cease and become absolutely void (without legal process) if the patentee fails within one year to introduce the invention into public use in the United States, or if after introduction the invention is not publicly used for six months, or if the patentee fails to become a citizen within the required period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides conditions under which patents granted to resident aliens intending to naturalize will automatically become void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of Patent Office and Commissioner of Patents; duties and custody
rubrics_metrics.description: An office denominated the Patent Office shall be attached to the Department of State; its chief officer called Commissioner of Patents shall be appointed by the President with Senate advice/consent, shall superintend and perform acts respecting granting and issuing patents, and have charge/custody of books, records, papers, models, machines, and other things belonging to the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner receives compensation equal to the Commissioner of Indian Department and is entitled to send/receive letters/packages by mail free of postage relating to office business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office staffing, salaries, and disqualification from private patent interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner may appoint chief clerk, examining clerk, clerks (one competent draughtsman), machinist, messenger with specified salaries; Commissioner, clerks, and persons appointed/employed in the office shall be disqualified and interdicted from acquiring or taking, except by inheritance, during their appointment period any right or interest, directly or indirectly, in any patent granted or to be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents conflicts of interest by forbidding office staff from having patent interests (except inheritance) during tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths, bonds, and fiscal accountability for office officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal officer and every person appointed shall make oath/affirmation to execute their trust faithfully; Commissioner and chief clerk shall each give bonds with sureties (Commissioner $10,000; chief clerk $5,000) conditioned to render true and faithful quarterly accounts to the Treasurer of moneys received for patent duties, copies, and other moneys received by virtue of office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures fiscal accountability for fees collected by the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal, certified copies, and fees for copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner shall provide a seal for the office; copies of records/drawings/papers signed by Commissioner (or chief clerk when office vacant) with seal affixed shall be competent evidence where originals could be evidence; applicants may obtain certified copies on payment—ten cents per 100 words for written copies and reasonable expense for copies of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies evidentiary weight of certified copies and fees for producing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and contents of patent; grant scope and term
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents shall be issued in the name of the Secretary of the United States under the Patent Office seal, signed by the Secretary and countersigned by the Commissioner, and recorded with descriptions/specifications/drawings; each patent shall contain a short description or title correctly indicating its nature and design, and shall grant to applicant (and heirs, administrators, executors, assigns) for a term not exceeding fourteen years the full and exclusive right and liberty of making, using, and vending the invention or discovery, referring to specifications annexed, and specifying what the patentee claims as his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formalities and the maximum statutory term (14 years) under this act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive patentability requirement — novelty and non-use by others
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person having discovered or invented a new and useful art, machine, manufacture, composition of matter, or useful improvement not known or used by others before his discovery/invention, and not at the time of application in public use or on sale with his consent or allowance, may apply for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be first/original discoverer and the subject not previously known/used; public use or sale with inventor's consent before application defeats patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification enabling requirement (written description; manner and process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any inventor shall receive a patent, he shall deliver a written description of his invention and of the manner and process of making, constructing, using, and compounding the same, in such full, clear, and exact terms, avoiding unnecessary prolixity, as to enable any person skilled in the art or science to which it appertains to make, construct, compound and use the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For machines, the inventor must fully explain the principle and several modes of applying that principle and particularly specify and point out the part, improvement, or combination claimed as his own invention or discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings, specimens, and models requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole shall be accompanied with a drawing or drawings and written references where the nature admits of drawings; or with specimens of ingredients/composition sufficient in quantity for experiment where the invention is of a composition of matter; descriptions and drawings signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses shall be filed; inventor shall also furnish a model in all cases which admit of representation by model of a convenient size to exhibit its parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies witness attestation and when models or specimens are appropriate; models required when invention lends itself to model representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination by Commissioner for prior art, public use, and utility/importance
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing the application, description, specification, and payment, the Commissioner shall make or cause to be made an examination of the alleged new invention; if it does not appear that the invention was invented/patented/described in printed publication or in public use/on sale prior to the applicant's alleged invention, and the Commissioner deems it sufficiently useful and important, it shall be his duty to issue a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Commissioner finds prior invention or defective/insufficient description, he shall notify applicant, giving useful information and references to consider renewing or altering specification to embrace only the new part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and process when specification/claim is defective or anticipation exists
rubrics_metrics.description: When examination shows the applicant was not the original and first inventor, or part of the claimed subject had been invented/discovered/patented/described before, or the description is defective/insufficient, the Commissioner shall notify the applicant and give brief information and references useful in deciding to renew, withdraw, or alter the specification to narrow claims to what is new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may withdraw and relinquish claim to the model to receive back $20 (part of duty) by filing written notice; if applicant persists, he must re‑swear and may obtain decision of a board of examiners upon payment and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of examiners appeal procedure and composition, fees and pay
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant persists after Commissioner’s objection, he may, on appeal and request in writing, have decision of a board of three disinterested persons appointed by the Secretary of State (one preferably skilled in the relevant art); board members under oath; applicant must pay $25 to institute the board; examiners may be paid not exceeding $10 each for services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board shall be furnished certificate of Commissioner’s decision and grounds; board gives reasonable notice to applicant and Commissioner to allow presentation of facts/evidence; board may reverse Commissioner's decision in whole or part and Commissioner shall be governed thereby.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interfering applications procedure and priority determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an application would, in Commissioner’s opinion, interfere with any other pending application or any unexpired patent, Commissioner must give notice to applicants/patentees; dissatisfied parties may appeal Commissioner’s decision on priority to a board of examiners under like terms and conditions, and like proceedings shall determine which applicant (if any) is entitled to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the act shall deprive an original inventor of right to patent because he previously took out letters-patent in a foreign country and the same had been published within six months preceding filing; applicant may request patent to date from filing time up to six months prior to issuing, and may request secret filing in archives until furnishing model (not exceeding one year) upon payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and patent fund (application and differential fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before consideration, applicant shall pay into the Treasury, Patent Office, or deposit bank: $30 if a citizen of the United States; $500 if a subject of the King of Great Britain; $300 for all other persons; duplicate receipts to be taken; moneys received shall constitute a patent fund for payment of salaries and other Patent Office expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies large differential fees for subjects of Great Britain and other foreigners and that sums form the Patent Office's operating fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and recordation requirement (timeframe and fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent is assignable in law by written instrument; such assignment, and every grant or conveyance of exclusive right under any patent (for whole or undivided part, or geographic portion), shall be recorded in the Patent Office within three months from execution, for which assignee or grantee shall pay the Commissioner $3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording assignment timely preserves public record of ownership and incurs a small recording fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing for delaying disclosure and securing priority (contents, fee, secrecy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen or eligible alien resident for one year and having sworn intention to become citizen who has invented a new art, machine, or improvement and desires further time may, on paying $20, file a caveat setting forth design, purpose, principal and distinguishing characteristics, praying protection until invention matured; caveat filed in confidential archives and preserved in secrecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another person applies for a patent within one year that may interfere, Commissioner deposits the description/specifications/drawings/model in confidential archives and mails notice to caveat filer, who has three months to file his full application to avail himself of the caveat; if specs interfere, like proceedings as in interfering applications may follow; caveat fee counts toward later application fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for inadvertent defects or overclaiming; fee and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of defective/insufficient description/specification or because the patentee claimed more than he had right to claim, if error arose by inadvertence/accident/mistake without fraudulent intention, the Commissioner, upon surrender of patent and payment of $15, may cause a new patent to be issued to the inventor for the residue of the unexpired period in accordance with corrected description and specification; similar right vests in executors/assignees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissued patent with corrected specification shall have same legal effect in actions thereafter as though originally filed in corrected form; patentee may likewise annex a subsequently invented improvement to the original patent on payment of $15 and proper proceedings.
